name: Joni Mitchell
hook: A Canadian singer-songwriter whose 1970 environmental anthem became, because she personally said yes, a Janet Jackson hit twenty-seven years later.
blurb: Joni Mitchell, born in Alberta, Canada, became one of the most admired singer-songwriters of the 1960s and 70s, known for lyrics that mixed personal detail with sharp observation. Her album 'Blue' (1971) set a standard for confessional songwriting in rock and folk that outlasted the singer-songwriter movement she came up in. Her 1970 song 'Big Yellow Taxi', about a parking lot paved over a paradise, was a fairly minor single for her, but it became her best-known crossing into hip-hop and R&B when it was sampled for Janet Jackson's 'Got 'til It's Gone' (1997). Jackson called Mitchell directly to ask permission, and Mitchell gave it and sang new vocals for the track herself.

signatureTracks.title: Big Yellow Taxi
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The source of the hook Janet Jackson sampled, and personally sang new vocals for, on 'Got 'til It's Gone'.
